target_customer: Independent physician associations, ACOs and primary care practices with risk-based or value-based contracts
problem: Primary care physicians lack bandwidth for background workflows such as screenings, prior authorizations, referrals and risk adjustment coding, which costs practices revenue and quality scores.
business_model: B2B software that sells AI agents operating inside the practice EHR; pricing not public
product_category: AI agents for primary care administrative workflows

founders.name: Mark Pothen
prior_employers: several early-stage healthcare startups (not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he grew up in his mother's primary care practice and spent six months embedded in a practice running its operations. Education not found on the YC page.

competitors.name: Commure
competitors.what: Healthcare AI platform with agents for front office, referral, intake and billing
competitors.funding_then: Reported $200M raise in the coverage cited

competitors.name: Notable
competitors.what: Workflow automation including authorization and care gap closure assistants
competitors.funding_then: Unverified reports of a Series B

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that operate multiple EHRs through the interface need reliability and compliance work, but computer-use models make the base capability available to a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow automations can be copied by well-funded platforms like Commure and Notable; the edge is depth in value-based care and embedded workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded platforms already sold similar agents by the batch start; no acquisition event found.

market_need_then: Physicians lack bandwidth for panel management; CMS rules effective 2026 push faster prior authorization decisions, and value-based contracts reward quality gap closure and risk adjustment coding. A first customer, an IPA with about 40,000 patients, went live per the YC page.

branding.domain_note: Uses beaconhealth.ai, not an exact .com; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional; headlines include Healthcare on Autopilot and The AI Workforce for Healthcare; mission line about bringing joy back to primary care

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is new, with only directory-style coverage found; the name is a common word shared with other health companies, so search confusion is likely.

outcome_analysis: Beacon Health is a Winter 2026 company with no outcome yet. It has a founder with firsthand primary care exposure and a technical co-founder, an early live deployment at an IPA, and a policy tailwind, but it competes with far better funded workflow automation platforms.
notes: Funding figures conflict across aggregators and none is verified: Dealroom lists $125K seed or $500K, one profile says $130K in January 2026, and Healthcare Discovery reports a Form D dated 2026-01-22 for a SAFE with $44,000 sold to 15 investors (not opened on EDGAR). No round recorded. Dealroom lists HQ as New York while YC lists San Francisco. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. No source on name origin or logo. Completeness pass: the 44K SAFE via an SPV (Form D dated 2026-01-22) rests on a single outlet (Healthcare Discovery). Dealroom's 125K or 500K and a 130K figure conflict and are not recorded, so the history may be incomplete.
